To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 10- bromobenzocyclopentapyridyl FTI Sch-66336 is a potent and orally bioavailable FTI.
indole substitution at C(10a) of the indolocyclheptapyridines results in a 3-5 fold improvement in potency over the benzocyclohepta- pyridines.
indolocyclopentapyridine FTI 10a is a potent, orally bioavailable FTI that is currently under clinical development for the treatment of solid tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, synthesis, structure, and pharmacological properties of a series of indolocycllohepta-pyridine farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) that are based upon the potent and selective 10-bromocyclloheptapyrindine FTIs, such as Sch-66336 [(+)-4].
the development of indolocyclheptapyridines as a new class of potent FTIs.
the design and synthesis of a series of FTIs based on the 10-bromocyclohepta- and indolocyclohexpa- substituted pyridine ring systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the indole group of (+)-10 is not the sole source of potency, but rather a combination of the 11-piperidyl substitutent, the conformational rigity of the 10-bromocycloheptyl moiety, and the hydrophobic interactions of the indole moiety are responsible for the observed potency of (+)-10.
the indole group in (+)-10 is responsible for the observed potency enhancement of (+)-10 compared with Sch-66336.

the indole moiety in (+) - 10a contributes to the observed increase in potency through increased hydrophobicity and conformational rigidi ty, while the 10-bromocycloheptyl moiety in 1 contributes to the increase in potency through conformational rigi dity and solvation effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the indolopyridine moiety provides a significant improvement in potency, while the 11- piperidyl moiety is not necessary for potency and is detrimental to pharmacokinetic properties.

the addition of the 10- bromo substituent to the benzocyclohepta moiety of FTI Sch-66336 provides a significant increase in potency through the addition of an entropic contribution to the binding process, as well as a significant increase in the hydrophobic interactions of the inhibitor with the protein.
the indolopyridine moiety of (+)-10 provides a more favorable binding mode to the protein than does the pyridyl moiety of (+) - 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of the hydrophobic indole ring to the cycloheptapyrindine moiety in Sch-66336 results in an increased potency in biochemical, cellular, and in vivo assays.
the 10-bromine group in 1 is important for potency but that the 11- piperidyl ring is more important for potency than previously realized.
a 10-substituent on benzocyclohepta[b]pyridine can be a powerful tool for improving the potency of an FTI.
